segments: Joining us now, Avi Loeb. He is a professor,
Harvard University, also the chair of the
White House's UAP Science Advisory Council.
So nice to see you. Good day to have you
here in Washington. Thanks for coming in.
Let's go back to those flying triangles.
What's your theory? What do you think?
Well, we don't know what they are. There are
two types of objects that are being spotted
by the Pentagon, the intelligence community,
and they are hovering over strategic assets.
We need to know what they are, because if
you have a down-to-earth approach, you would
say they are coming from adversarial nations,
because it's not our government that is
flying them.
And we shut down a Chinese pie balloon in
2023, and when I go to the kitchen and find
an ant,
I get worried because there must be many
more ants under the sink.
So for the same reason, we need to figure
out these objects.
Now, we won't be able to, given the data
that we're given in these tranches, it's not
good enough.
And my hope is to partner with the Pentagon
and put better sensors at the locations
where these objects are found.
You were at the White House today.
How are you?
